chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

Regarding the hunting of the dog: if its owner releases it and mentions the name of Allah, then let him eat all that it holds for him, even if it kills. And if it ate from it, then eat what remains. And if it was not trained, but he trained it at that moment when he releases it, then let him eat from it, for it is trained.

But as for what is other than dogs, among that which cheetahs, falcons, and the like hunt, do not eat from its catch except what you reach in time for its proper slaughter, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:
So whatever is other than dogs, its catch is not of that which may be eaten unless you reach its proper slaughter.

key_terms.أَمْسَكَ: seized or held the prey for the hunter
key_terms.الْفُهُودُ: cheetahs or hunting felines used to catch prey
key_terms.الْكَلْبِ: the hunting dog whose catch is under discussion
key_terms.سَمَّىٰ: mentioned the name of Allah at the time of release

ai.seo_question: Is game caught by a hunting dog halal to eat, and does the same ruling apply to falcons and cheetahs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on game caught by hunting animals. It permits eating what a dog catches when it is released by its owner with the name of Allah mentioned, while excluding the catch of other hunting animals and birds unless the animal is reached alive and properly slaughtered. The ruling is linked to the Qur'anic wording "مُكَلِّبِينَ," indicating trained hunting dogs specifically.
